messages:
support-ryan: Heads up — Acme reported intermittent decrypt timeouts from staging: ~3-5% of /v1/generate requests are failing with a KMS decrypt timeout and the client retries are causing a billing spike. Happening since their key rotation 6h ago. sample request-id: r-0a1b2c3d.

alice: can you paste the CloudTrail decrypt event (requestID + eventTime) and the exact KMS KeyId they use? also which SDK/version and whether they're using envelope encryption?

kms-bot: [alert] KMS API latency spike detected in us-west-2 (Decrypt 95p latency > 800ms) — recent spike at 2026-03-17T09:12:30Z.

dinesh: curious — rotation + encryptionContext mismatch has bitten us before. if client rotates wrapping key but still sends old encryptionContext it can fall back to slower HSM path. ask Acme to confirm encryptionContext exactly matches the one used at encrypt time.

carla: repro steps I want everyone to try locally: run the aws cli decrypt against the same KeyId + encryptionContext. example:
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234 --encryption-context '{"tenant":"acme-prod"}' --region us-west-2 --debug
```
that will show if KMS returns TLS/timeout or a successful payload. please capture the x-amzn-RequestId and HTTP roundtrip timing.

ben: also verify they're connecting from the same VPC endpoint vs internet. proxy TLS handshakes or NAT gateway CPU can add tens to hundreds ms and cause client-side timeouts + retries.

support-ryan: attaching minimal logline from Acme (sanitized):
`2026-03-17T09:11:29Z ERROR decrypt timeout requestId=r-0a1b2c3d sdk=js v3 retries=2 keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-1234`

alice: please also pull CloudTrail event with that x-amzn-RequestId. looking for whether KMS responded with Throttling or an error like InvalidCiphertext or a successful response but delayed. if CloudTrail shows Decrypt completed but >1s, it's KMS side. if there is no Decrypt event, request may be blocked by IAM or proxy.

kms-bot: CloudTrail snapshot for r-0a1b2c3d: Decrypt event present at 2026-03-17T09:11:29.832Z — status: Success. latency_ms: 1127. encryptionContext: {tenant=acme-prod}. keyRotationStatus: rotation-pending?

dinesh: 1. rotation-pending is interesting (in-flight rotation can touch HSM state). 2. 1.1s decrypt suggests KMS internal HSM path — normal for cross-account grants sometimes. check if they used a grant vs key policy.

carla: can you have Acme run this narrow reproducer in their staging where they saw failures and include SDK debug logs and environment (VPC endpoint vs public):
- Capture TCP RTT to kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
- Run aws kms decrypt as above with --debug
- If using envelope libs, dump the encryptionContext exactly as sent

ben: one more ask — get the customer's STS session policy if they use AssumeRole with session policies. IAM conditions can strip encryptionContext via condition keys and cause KMS to route differently.

zoe: from compliance side we also need to confirm no audit log gaps. please export CloudTrail for the 1h window around the spike and upload to the secure bucket (s3://redwood-internal-escalations/acme/2112345678). tag me @zoe when uploaded.

support-ryan: Acme confirmed they rotated the data key wrapping key 6h ago and used the same encryptionContext. They provided an example aws decrypt debug; pasted the requestId x-amz = r-0a1b2c3d. I will upload the debug logs to the bucket.

alice: I'm going to run the CLI repro against the same KeyId from a host in our VPC to rule out network. If we reproduce, we'll open a KMS support case with AWS (provide requestId and CloudTrail slice). If we can't reproduce, likely client environment (NAT/proxy).

kms-bot: quick note — KMS quota for Decrypt in key/abcd-1234 is below threshold. no quota denies recorded in last 24h.

dinesh: if AWS escalation is needed, include: RequestIDs (KMS + CloudTrail), snapshot of key rotation schedule, grant vs policy usage, encryptionContext, and a short timeline showing when rotation occurred vs first failures. AWS tends to correlate HSM slow paths with rotation windows.

carla: sample IAM repro command if you suspect session policy is dropping context:
```python
import boto3
kms = boto3.client('kms', region_name='us-west-2')
resp = kms.decrypt(CiphertextBlob=open('blob.bin','rb').read(), EncryptionContext={'tenant':'acme-prod'})
print(resp)
```
run with AWS_PROFILE pointed at the same role that Acme uses.

ben: ops note — if we find an internal KMS proxy (we don't normally proxy KMS calls), ensure no TCP keepalive timeouts or HTTP/2 connection resets are happening. those cause long tails and client retries.

zoe: I'll kick off an internal compliance audit for the CloudTrail retention for that customer's resources while we investigate — want to ensure we have full coverage for any repro.

support-ryan: uploaded logs to s3://redwood-internal-escalations/acme/2112345678 and shared read ACL with eng-security. please check and I'll rotate the upload link if needed.

alice: will run repro now from our VPC host and post results. thanks everyone.

support-ryan: thanks team — I'll hold the customer open and escalate to AWS if we reproduce. will update in this thread. :thumbsup:
